title: The approval limits by decision, product and amount are not set, so no approval requirement can be tested against its limit
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 section 9 (DL18 open); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features FEAT-VAL-08, FEAT-VAL-09, FEAT-TRT-03, FEAT-AST-16, FEAT-WOF-06; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Settlement route set R-SET-05; Template and Rules v1 R3
section: 8 Business requirements BR-002, BR-020, BR-028, BR-040, BR-053, BR-073; 9 RULE-011; 12 Q-001
description: Every approval requirement in Epics 3 to 8 refers to a delegated limit held in the delegation of authority table, and DL18 is open: the source says to load the regulation's levels now and to add names and substitutes when they are signed. No source states a limit, a currency threshold, a product split or a substitute for any decision, so the approval path, the escalation and the committee threshold cannot be tested with a business value.
evidence: Program BRD v4 section 9 DL18 'Load the regulation's levels and limits now; add names and substitutes when signed'; R-SET-05 routes an offer below the floor to the approval committee with no amount; FEAT-WOF-06 approves a write-off inside the delegation with no limit stated
proposed: Load the regulation's published levels as reference data in the version that applies at the release date, keep every limit and substitute as a versioned row with a valid-from date, and let each acceptance criterion run against the loaded version. No limit is written in this document, in a story or in code.

title: The settlement range and the floor price basis per product are not specified
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Settlement route set R-SET-04, R-SET-05, R-SET-09; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-VAL-06, FEAT-TRT-02, FEAT-TRT-03
section: 8 Business requirements BR-002, BR-018; 9 RULE-003; 12 Q-002
description: Requirements BR-002 and BR-018 depend on a settlement range low and high and on a floor price that the rules compare an offer against. The sources name the parameters and say the range comes from reference data with the floor applied, but no source gives the range, the floor basis, the product split or the rounding.
evidence: R-SET-04 condition 'offer_amount between settlement_range_low and settlement_range_high'; R-SET-05 condition 'offer_amount < floor_price'; FEAT-VAL-06 'settlement range from the rules, with the floor applied'; no value in any source
proposed: Hold the range and the floor as versioned reference rows per product and effective date, load a documented test version for SIT, and let the business owner approve the production version in the same way as the treatment policy.

title: The offer validity, cure period, maximum breaks and queue and approval timers are named as parameters but not valued
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-RES-09, R-RES-27, R-RES-29, R-RES-30; Program BRD v4 section 9 DL22 and DL23; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-TRT-07, FEAT-TRT-11
section: 8 Business requirements BR-004, BR-006; 9 RULE-004, RULE-005; 12 Q-003
description: The rules carry an offer validity of 14 days in two rows, but the cure period, the maximum number of breaks and the queue and approval service levels are written as parameters with no value. DL22 and DL23 are open. A timer requirement cannot be tested without its value, and the two 14 day rows are not confirmed as the policy.
evidence: R-RES-09 'offer validity 14 days'; R-RES-27 'cure_period_days from reference data'; R-RES-30 'break_count < max_breaks'; Program BRD v4 DL22 'Load the values as parameters'; DL23 'Load as parameters'
proposed: Load every timer as a versioned parameter row with a valid-from date; use the 14 day offer validity the rules state as the documented test value, and leave the cure period, the maximum breaks and the service levels to the approved load DL22 and DL23 name.

title: The statutory notice periods and the litigation step service levels are not specified
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Litigation route set R-LIT-01 to R-LIT-79; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-LIT-01, FEAT-LIT-03; Program BRD v4 REQ-CWC-012 and REQ-S4-001
description: A notice period timer and a prescription warning are requirements, and both read a legal period from the legal periods table. No source gives the notice period for mortgage, hire purchase or SSME, or the service level for each litigation step, so the timer and the warning cannot be tested against a business value.
evidence: R-LIT rows carry timers such as 'notice_period from legal periods'; REQ-CWC-012 'Prescription dates are set from the legal periods table at case creation'; no period is stated in any source
proposed: Hold the legal periods and the litigation service levels in the legal periods reference table, load the periods Legal signs, and test the timer against the loaded version rather than a literal.

title: The provision step thresholds and the held-asset re-appraisal interval are not specified
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-AST-05, FEAT-AST-09; Program BRD v4 REQ-S5-003
section: 8 Business requirements BR-010, BR-011; 9 RULE-001; 12 Q-005
description: Holding age drives a provision step at each threshold and a re-appraisal order at the re-appraisal interval, and both values are policy parameters. No source states a threshold, a step size, a percentage or an interval, so the provision requirement cannot be tested and the asset cannot be valued at a point in time.
evidence: FEAT-AST-05 'applies the provision step the policy sets at each threshold'; FEAT-AST-09 'when the holding period passes the re-appraisal interval'; no value in any source
proposed: Hold the thresholds, the steps and the interval as versioned parameters owned by the NPA business owner, and let the provision and re-appraisal criteria run against the loaded version with the value visible on the asset record.

title: The write-off tax criteria and the meaning of the two tracks are not specified
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-WOF-01, FEAT-WOF-02; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Write-off route set R-WO-01 to R-WO-51; Program BRD v4 REQ-S7-001
description: The monthly scan runs on both tracks and tests every proposed account against the tax criteria. The sources name neither track and state no tax criterion, so the population cannot be reproduced and the tax position cannot be defended to an auditor or to the Revenue Department.
evidence: FEAT-WOF-01 'on both tracks'; FEAT-WOF-02 'tests each proposed account against the tax criteria'; no criterion or track name in any source
proposed: Hold the two tracks and the tax criteria as one versioned rule package with its test cases, name the tracks in the version label, and let the scan report the version it applied.

title: The write-off exception loop has no named owner and no time limit
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-WOF-12; Program BRD v4 REQ-S7-004; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Write-off route set
description: The specification says the exception loop has no owner today and the program requirement asks for one named owner and a time limit, and no source names the role or the limit. The requirement can therefore state the duty but cannot name the owner it is owed to.
evidence: FEAT-WOF-12 'Opens the exception path for a case the rules cannot clear. This loop has no owner today'; REQ-S7-004 'has one named owner and a time limit'; no role or limit stated
proposed: Assign the loop to the write-off team with an escalation to the team manager after the time limit the business sets, and record the unmapped owner as a gap until the role is confirmed.

title: Enforcement after judgment and the eviction of a held property have no named owner role
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-LIT-20, FEAT-AST-08; Program BRD v4 REQ-S4-007, REQ-S4-008
section: 8 Business requirements BR-026, BR-041; 9 RULE-026; 12 Q-008
description: The specification states that enforcement after judgment has no owner today and that an eviction needs Legal with no legal owner today, and the program requirement asks for one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement. The source gives the duty and the gap but not the role that holds it.
evidence: FEAT-LIT-20 'Enforcement after judgment has no owner today'; FEAT-AST-08 'which needs Legal and has no legal owner today'; REQ-S4-007 'has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement'
proposed: Use the enforcement owner role the rules already name for enforcement, with Legal counsel named on an eviction, and record the assignment as an assumption until the operating model names the holder.

title: The non performing asset stock balance has no named owner
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-AST-06; Program BRD v4 REQ-S5-002
description: The specification says the asset stock balance has no owner today, and the program requirement asks for one named owner and a monthly report. The source does not name the role, so the monthly report has no accountable recipient in the requirements.
evidence: FEAT-AST-06 'Gives the stock balance an owner and a number on one screen. It has no owner today'; REQ-S5-002 'has one named owner and is reported monthly'
proposed: Name the NPA and asset manager as the role that owns the stock position per case, with the head of NPA as the recipient of the monthly report, and confirm both in the operating model.

title: The debt sale cap is stated as a percentage with no basis, period or measurement
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-DBS-01, FEAT-DBS-16; Program BRD v4 REQ-S6-001
section: 8 Business requirements BR-044, BR-050; 9 RULE-015; 12 Q-010
description: The specification names a 54 percent cap in the eligibility rule and asks for the headroom to be reported. No source states what the 54 percent applies to, over what period it is measured, or which population is the denominator, so headroom cannot be computed or reported.
evidence: FEAT-DBS-01 'including the 54 percent cap'; FEAT-DBS-16 'Holds the sale population inside the policy cap and reports the headroom'; no denominator, period or basis in any source
proposed: Hold the cap as a versioned policy parameter with its basis and period in the version label, compute headroom against the population the policy names, and report the version used with each lot.

title: The buyer licensing and eligibility criteria and the authority that bars a buyer are not specified
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-DBS-06, FEAT-DBS-07; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Debt sale route set R-DS-15; Program BRD v4 REQ-S6-004, REQ-S6-005
description: A buyer must pass KYC, licensing and eligibility checks before it bids, and a licence breach removes it from the panel. No source states which licences, which thresholds, which evidence, or which role may bar a buyer and on whose approval.
evidence: FEAT-DBS-06 'Runs the KYC, licensing and eligibility checks before a buyer can bid'; FEAT-DBS-07 'Removes a buyer from the panel on a license breach'; R-DS-15 condition 'kyc_status = passed and licence_expiry after today and panel_status = active'
proposed: Reuse the bank's existing KYC and licensing checks, hold the accepted licence types and their validity as reference data, and let the debt sale officer bar a buyer with Compliance confirming the reason.

title: Retention periods and masking rules by record class and role are not set
source: Program BRD v4 section 9 DL26 and NFR-028, NFR-030, NFR-031, NFR-043; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-COM-08, FEAT-WOF-13, FEAT-ADM-11
section: 8 Business requirements BR-032, BR-057, BR-079; 9 RULE-028; 12 Q-012
description: Retention is a requirement for documents, the decision log, the interaction ledger and a case, and the sources state that the periods are not set and that DL26 is open. Masking by role is required and the fields and roles are not stated either, so a disposal or a data subject request cannot be proved.
evidence: NFR-028 'Retention classes defined per type; periods not set'; NFR-030 'Log retention is set by Compliance'; Program BRD v4 DL26 'Provide per data product and document type'
proposed: Hold a retention class and a masking rule per record class and role as versioned reference data, apply the class at creation, and record every disposal as a decision so a period that is not yet set cannot be breached silently.

title: The TCG quota and the claim deadline for each scheme are not specified
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-GUA-01, FEAT-GUA-02, integration INT-29; Program BRD v4 REQ-S3-001
description: A guarantee claim must be filed inside the scheme deadline and against the scheme quota, and the integration row says the TCG interface is not available today and is entered by the guarantee officer. No source states the deadline or the quota per scheme, so the claim timer and the quota check cannot be tested.
evidence: FEAT-GUA-01 'Assembles the claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires'; INT-29 'Not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer'; no deadline or quota stated
proposed: Hold the quota and the deadline per scheme as reference data, show the remaining quota and the remaining days on the claim, and let the officer file manually until the TCG interface is available.

title: The evidence and threshold for raising or lowering an agent autonomy level are not specified
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-AGT-12, FEAT-AGT-15; Program BRD v4 REQ-ACA-010; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-066
section: 8 Business requirements BR-015, BR-084; 9 RULE-029; 12 Q-014
description: An autonomy level may be raised on measured evidence and dropped on a breach, and no source states which measure, which threshold, which period or which approval each change needs. The requirement can therefore be met only by inventing a threshold, which the run rules forbid.
evidence: FEAT-AGT-15 'Steps an agent up on measured evidence, and drops it on a breach, with the approval each needs'; NFR-066 'Agent acceptance, override rate, latency and cost are measured and reported' with no threshold
proposed: Hold the measure, the threshold and the approval level per agent and per decision as a versioned row, keep the first autonomy level at its current setting, and let the committee set the threshold before any step-up is taken.

title: The deceased customer flow is placed in Epic 3 by the program requirement and in Epic 7 by the specification and the stories
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.15 REQ-DVH-008 (Epic E3); Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features sheet FEAT-DVF-03 (E7) and story RWB-E7-003; User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3 'Run X3 deceased customer end to end'
description: REQ-DVH-008 states that a death stops all contact, notifies the heirs and starts the insurance claim path, and tags the requirement to Epic 3. The specification places the same capability in Epic 7 as FEAT-DVF-03, and the story master holds it as RWB-E7-003. Read as written, one business need sits in two releases, and E3 would release without the capability its program requirement claims.
evidence: Program BRD v4 section 5.15 row REQ-DVH-008 with Epic E3; Specification v3 features sheet row FEAT-DVF-03 with Epic E7; User Stories master heading RWB-E7-003
proposed: Read the requirement as an E7 deviation flow served by RWB-E7-003, and record in the E3 scope that the death and estate capability is delivered in E7. No story moves between epics without the Product Owner's decision.

title: Epic 3 features depend on Epic 4 features that release a month later
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features sheet: FEAT-TRT-02 (E3) depends on FEAT-VAL-06 (E4), FEAT-VAL-02 depends on FEAT-VAL-01 (E4), FEAT-AST-09 (E3) depends on FEAT-VAL-01 (E4); User Stories master RWB-E3-002, RWB-E3-026
section: 8 Business requirements BR-002, BR-018, BR-020; 7.3; 12 Q-016
description: The specification's dependency column shows E3 features waiting on E4 features: the settlement offer needs the payoff and settlement range, and the held-asset re-appraisal needs the appraisal order. E3 releases on 31 January 2027 and E4 on 28 February 2027, so as written E3 cannot meet its own acceptance criteria at its release.
evidence: Features sheet: FEAT-TRT-02 'Depends on FEAT-TRT-01, FEAT-VAL-06' with Epic E3; FEAT-VAL-06 with Epic E4; FEAT-AST-09 Epic E3 'Depends on FEAT-VAL-01' Epic E4
proposed: Read the E3 stories as building against the published valuation contract and its fake, and move the two valuation features the E3 stories need into the E3 release, or accept that those two E3 criteria are signed off in E4. The choice belongs to the Product Owner and the solution architect.

title: An Epic 3 feature depends on an Epic 8 administration feature
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features sheet FEAT-AGT-12 (E3) depends on FEAT-CWC-22 (E8); User Stories master RWB-E3-030 and RWB-E8-006
description: Changing an autonomy level is an E3 feature and its stated dependency is the configuration feature that administrative screens deliver in E8, five months later. As written, the E3 feature cannot be used in E3, and the E8 administration screen would be built to satisfy a story already released.
evidence: Features sheet FEAT-AGT-12 Epic E3 'Depends on FEAT-CWC-22'; FEAT-CWC-22 Epic E8; RWB-E3-030 'as a versioned configuration row'
proposed: Serve the E3 autonomy change through the configuration path delivered in Epic 1 and the approvals path delivered in Epic 2, and let the E8 screen present the same rows. No second store is created for autonomy.

title: The regulatory return feature names a data lake that the target architecture removes
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-RPT-07 systems column 'Power BI, Data lake'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 2 and ADR-018 (no data lake); Program BRD v4 REQ-DRI-009 and NFR-032
description: The regulatory return feature lists the data lake as its source, and the target architecture removes the data lake: reporting reads events, and the copy of the decision log to the lake is retired. Read as written, the return would read a store that does not exist in the target.
evidence: FEAT-RPT-07 'Builds the regulatory extracts from the data products and the decision log' with systems 'Power BI, Data lake'; Architecture v5 slide 2 'ACE database; no data lake connection'; ADR-018; REQ-DRI-009 'The decision log is copied to the data lake copy daily'
proposed: Read the return as built from the reporting read model and the central decision log, with no lake in the path, and keep the requirement ID and the measure unchanged.

title: Partner instruction is an Epic 4 endpoint in the specification and an Epic 6 feature in the same specification
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 APIs sheet rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions and the three partner instruction rows tagged E4; features sheet FEAT-PRM-03, FEAT-PRM-05 tagged E6
description: The API sheet places the partner instruction endpoints in Epic 4, and the feature sheet places the allocation and result features that use them in Epic 6. The story master holds no E4 partner instruction story, so the E4 endpoints have no story in E4 and the E6 features have no endpoint of their own.
evidence: APIs sheet rows tagged E4 for /cases/{caseId}/instructions and /partner/instructions; features sheet FEAT-PRM-03 and FEAT-PRM-05 tagged E6; user story master holds RWB-E6-031 and RWB-E6-033 only
proposed: Keep the instruction endpoints where the contract publishes them in E4 and let the E6 features consume the same contract, so the endpoint is built once and the allocation rules arrive in E6.

title: The benefit model measures and baselines are named but not given
source: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-RPT-06; Program BRD v4 section 2 and section 9
description: Benefit realisation tracks the measures in the benefit model against the baseline every month, and no source gives the benefit model measures or their baselines. The eight program measures are given with today and target values and are not the same set.
evidence: FEAT-RPT-06 'Tracks the measures in the benefit model against the baseline, monthly'; Program BRD v4 section 2 gives eight measures; no benefit model document in the read-only set
proposed: Report the eight program measures from section 2 until the benefit model is supplied, and label the report as the program measure set, not the benefit model.

title: The debt sale service wave is earlier than the business epic wave that awards a lot
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 wave map (EP05 and EP06 wave 4 for EP06, EP05 wave 3); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (S6 rwb-debtsale wave 3)
description: The debt sale service is created in wave 3 while the E6 award and write-off epic is in wave 4, and the E5 lot building in wave 3 depends on the same service. The wave map rule keeps the earlier wave for a story, so the ordering has to be stated explicitly or the lot and award stories fall into one lane with no stated cut.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 S6 wave 3; Template and Rules v1 R5.6 table EP06 wave 4; E5 lot features FEAT-DBS-01 to FEAT-DBS-04 in E5
proposed: Build the S6 service contract and the lot features in wave 3 with E5, and build the award, transfer and posting features in wave 4 with E6, on the same service and the same schema.

title: The debt sale turnaround has a target and no baseline
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 section 2 measures table
description: The program measures table gives the debt sale turnaround as 45 days with no baseline value, so the improvement cannot be shown and the measure cannot be closed at release.
evidence: Program BRD v4 section 2 row 'Debt sale turnaround | No baseline | 45 days'
proposed: Measure the current cycle on the first lot of the release and publish it as the baseline with the target of 45 days unchanged.

title: First-time-right on case packs and write-off returns has a target and no baseline
source: Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-037
description: The quality target of 90 percent first-time-right is stated for case packs and write-off returns, and no baseline or sample size is given, so the QA sample cannot show an improvement or a regression.
evidence: NFR-037 'Quality assurance reaches first-time-right on case packs and write-off returns | 90 percent'
proposed: Publish the first QA sample as the baseline and measure each later sample against it, with the sample rule recorded next to the measure.

title: Document classification accuracy has a target and no baseline
source: Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-017
description: Classification is measured at 90 percent correct on the labelled sample, and no labelled sample size or current accuracy is given in the sources, so the measure cannot show a change.
evidence: NFR-017 'Document classification is correct on the labeled sample | 90 percent correct'
proposed: Record the labelled sample and its size with the first measurement, and publish each later measurement against the same sample definition.

title: The override rate is reported monthly with no target
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.7 REQ-APD-005 and section 5.15 REQ-S8-006
description: A coded override reason is reported monthly and the sources set no target for the rate, so the measure can be published but not judged.
evidence: REQ-APD-005 'the reason is reported monthly'; REQ-S8-006 'Override and deviation patterns are reviewed monthly'; no target in any source
proposed: Publish the override rate by decision and product with the reason mix, and let the review forum set the target after the first three months of data.

title: Agent acceptance, override, latency and cost are measured with no target and no baseline
source: Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-066
description: Agent measures are required per agent and no target, baseline or reporting period is stated, so the measure cannot close the agent risk review at the committee.
evidence: NFR-066 'Agent acceptance, override rate, latency and cost are measured and reported | Measured per agent'
proposed: Report the four measures per agent and per decision from the agent run record, and let the model risk owner set the targets before the first autonomy step-up.

title: The daily case list reconciliation has no variance tolerance
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 NFR-018 and section 9 DL25; REQ-RDF-007
description: The case list must reconcile to the ACE account view with no unexplained variance, and DL25 is the open decision on the tolerance per data product. Without a tolerance, every rounding difference is an exception and the measure cannot be met.
evidence: NFR-018 'No unexplained variance; tolerance per data product under DL25'; Program BRD v4 DL25
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner
proposed: Report the variance by data product with no tolerance until DL25 is decided, and apply the agreed tolerance by version once it is set.
